findings.title: Missing prisma import causes ReferenceError
findings.body: packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts uses prisma.credential.update at line 96 but never imports prisma. Every Salesforce getClient call will throw ReferenceError and break all Salesforce calendar operations, and TypeScript build fails.

findings.title: Stores Zod safeParse wrapper instead of token data
findings.body: In packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the full safeParse result {success, data}. The code stores that wrapper as credential.key instead of .data. The next load via googleCredentialSchema.parse will fail because the stored shape is {success,data} not tokens, corrupting Google credentials after first refresh.

findings.title: Placeholder refresh_token overwrites real refresh token
findings.body: parseRefreshTokenResponse injects refresh_token='refresh_token' literal when missing. The PR docs say the external sync endpoint returns only access_token and expiry. Callers in Office365, Zoom and Webex persist that object, overwriting the valid stored refresh_token with the dummy string and permanently destroying the ability to refresh via the provider.

findings.title: Lenient token schema uses broken computed keys and strips fields
findings.body: minimumTokenResponseSchema uses [z.string().toString()] as object keys, which evaluates to a literal string like Zod object toString, not a wildcard. Zod by default strips unknown keys, so expiry_date, expires_in, instance_url, signature and other required fields are dropped. Downstream merges then lose expiry and Salesforce loses instance_url, corrupting credentials.

findings.title: Sync path returns fetch Response but code expects .data
findings.body: When credential sync is enabled refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response. Google code does res?.data expecting a Gaxios response with .data. fetch Response has no .data, so token is undefined and token.access_token throws TypeError, breaking Google refresh for all sync-enabled users.

findings.title: Sync response treated as HubspotToken without parsing
findings.body: Hubspot refresh expects a HubspotToken object from hubspotClient.oauth.tokensApi.createToken. When sync is enabled refreshOAuthTokens returns a fetch Response. The code then reads .expiresIn/.accessToken directly from the Response and computes expiryDate as NaN, storing invalid tokens and breaking Hubspot integration.

findings.title: Passes credentialId as calcomUserId to sync endpoint
findings.body: zoho-bigin refreshAccessToken receives credentialId which is credential.id and passes it as the userId argument to refreshOAuthTokens, which sends it as calcomUserId. The sync endpoint will look up the wrong user or fail, returning wrong tokens. It should pass credential.userId like all other calendar services.

findings.title: Assumes axios shape but sync path returns fetch Response
findings.body: Bigin code does tokenInfo.data.error assuming an axios response. When sync is enabled refreshOAuthTokens returns a fetch Response which has no .data, so tokenInfo.data is undefined and accessing .error throws TypeError, breaking Bigin refresh in sync mode.

findings.title: Assumes axios shape but sync path returns fetch Response
findings.body: Zohocrm code does zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.error assuming axios. When sync is enabled refreshOAuthTokens returns a fetch Response with no .data, so .data.error throws TypeError. The sync response is never parsed via .json(), breaking Zoho CRM refresh.

findings.title: Sync response fed to Lark-specific error parser
findings.body: Lark refresh passes the result of refreshOAuthTokens to handleLarkError which expects a Lark envelope {code:0,data:{...}}. The sync endpoint is documented to return only access_token and expiry, so the parser will throw even on success, breaking Lark refresh when sync is enabled. Sync path needs separate parsing.

findings.title: Returns connection with stale tokens after refresh
findings.body: After refreshing and updating the DB with accessTokenParsed.data, Salesforce getClient builds the jsforce.Connection from the old credentialKey.access_token and credentialKey.instance_url instead of the new tokens. All subsequent Salesforce calls use the expired token until the credential is reloaded.

findings.title: Checks statusText instead of status code
findings.body: Salesforce refresh checks response.statusText !== 'OK' to detect failure. statusText is an optional reason phrase that varies by server and is often empty. It should check !response.ok or response.status. The current check causes false failures or missed failures.

findings.title: Bypasses sync helper yet uses lenient schema
findings.body: Unlike every other service, Salesforce getClient always fetches Salesforce directly and never calls refreshOAuthTokens, so sync mode is ineffective. Worse, when sharing is enabled parseRefreshTokenResponse uses the lenient schema that strips instance_url/signature/scope, and the truncated object is persisted, corrupting Salesforce credentials.

findings.title: Wrong appSlug sent to sync endpoint for Zoom
findings.body: Zoom refresh passes appSlug 'zoomvideo' but the DB appId and credential type use 'zoom' and 'zoom_video'. All other services pass the DB slug. The sync endpoint receiving 'zoomvideo' will not match the Zoom app and cannot return tokens, breaking Zoom refresh in sync mode. It should be 'zoom'.

findings.title: Mutating webhook allows any HTTP method
findings.body: The app-credential webhook creates/overwrites user credentials but never checks req.method. GET, HEAD and other methods can mutate state, exposing encrypted keys in logs/caches and enabling CSRF. It should reject non-POST with 405.

findings.title: Unhandled Zod decrypt and JSON errors return 500
findings.body: The webhook calls zod .parse, symmetricDecrypt and JSON.parse without try/catch. Invalid body, wrong encryption key or non-JSON plaintext throws and results in unhandled 500 instead of 400, and can crash the handler. It should use safeParse and handle decrypt failures.

findings.title: Webhook header lookup not normalized to lowercase
findings.body: Node lowercases incoming header names, but the code looks up req.headers[process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME] verbatim. If the operator configures an uppercase header name the lookup always misses and all valid webhooks return 403. The env value should be lowercased before lookup.

findings.title: Find-then-create race can duplicate credentials
findings.body: The webhook does findFirst then update or create as two separate queries. Concurrent webhook deliveries for the same user and app can both miss and both create, leaving duplicate credentials where later reads use findFirst arbitrarily. It should use an atomic upsert or transaction.

findings.title: Sync fetch has no auth, no error check and no fallback
findings.body: refreshOAuthTokens POSTs calcomUserId and appSlug to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT with no secret/HMAC, no Content-Type, no response.ok check and no fallback to direct provider refresh. If the endpoint is down or returns an error, refresh fails even though the provider would succeed, causing availability regression, and the unauthenticated callback is spoofable.

findings.title: Overwrites expiry_date even when sync returns it
findings.body: Office365 video always sets expiry_date from expires_in with fallback 0. If the sync endpoint returns expiry_date instead of expires_in, the valid expiry is overwritten with approximately Date.now(), causing immediate expiry and a refresh loop. It should preserve an existing expiry_date.

findings.title: Sharing flag is string not boolean
findings.body: APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is assigned process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET && process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY, which is a string or undefined, not a boolean. Strict boolean checks will misbehave. It should be coerced with Boolean or !!.
